text:
<meta>continues from previous page: ...aid the purgations of women.</meta> and the application of its juice. Olympias of Thebes added hyssop and nitre. The ash of stag horn taken as a drink. Likewise for a laboring womb. Also, apply bull bile with opium, two obols in weight. It is beneficial to fumigate the womb with stag hair. They report that stags, when they sense they are pregnant, swallow a small stone, which is found in their excrement or in the womb (for it is also found there), and is guarded by being tied on. Small bones are also found in the heart and womb, which are very useful for pregnant women and those in labor. Regarding the pumice stone, which is found in the uterus of cows in a similar way, we have spoken in the nature of oxen. Applied wolf fat softens the womb. Its liver relieves their pains. Eating the meat of a wolf is beneficial for those about to give birth. Or if it is nearby when they begin to labor, it is effective, even against harmful applications. However, for it to arrive after the labor has begun is dangerous. The hare is also of great use to women. Its dried lung, taken as a drink, aids the womb. Its liver with Samian earth in water as a drink is for discharges. Its rennet is for the afterbirth. They avoid baths on the previous day. Also, applied with saffron and leek juice, and inserted in wool, it expels dead fetuses. If the wombs of hares are eaten, they believe it causes the conception of males. This is also achieved by their testicles and rennet. A fetus removed from a hare's uterus is said to bring lasting fertility to those who have ceased to bear children. But also, it is healthy before conception for the man to drink it. Likewise, nine grains of dung for a virgin so that her breasts may remain firm forever. Also with the rennet. For this reason, they smear it with honey where they do not want hair to grow back after it has been plucked. For inflation of the womb, apply boar or pig dung with oil. It stops discharges more effectively if it is flour of the dried substance or sprinkled in a potion, or if pregnant women or those who have just given birth are in pain. Drinking sow's milk with honeyed wine aids the labor of women. Taken by itself, it replenishes the failing milk of those who have just given birth. The same substance, when smeared on with the blood of a female pig, causes the breasts to grow less. If they ache, they are soothed by drinking ass's milk. Taken with added honey, it also aids their purgations. The aged tallow of the same animal also heals ulcerations of the womb, and when applied in wool, it softens the hardness of the womb. Used fresh or aged, applied with water, it has the power of a <term>psilothrum</term> <gloss>hair-removing agent</gloss>. The aged spleen of the same animal, applied with water, increases the abundance of breast milk. Fumigation corrects the womb. Fumigated donkey hooves hasten labor, so as even to induce an abortion; it is not used in any other way than this, which kills the living fetus. If fresh dung of the same animal is applied, it is said to stop blood discharges remarkably well. Also, the ash of the same dung, which, when applied, is also beneficial to the womb. Horse foam applied for forty days before the first hairs appear causes them to cease. Likewise, a decoction of stag horn. It is better if the horns are fresh. The womb is washed and aided by mare's milk. If the fetus is felt to be dead, the spleen, drunk in sweet water, expels it. Likewise, fumigation with hooves or dried dung. Butter infused stops a prolapsed womb. Bull bile mixed with rose oil opens a hardened womb; apply it externally in wool with terebinth resin. They also say that by the fumigation of bull dung, prolapsed wombs are checked, and labor is aided. But conception is aided by drinking cow's milk. It is certain that sterility occurs because of the strain of labor. Olympias of Thebes affirms that this is corrected by bull bile, snake fat, and verdigris, added to honey, and applied to the affected areas before intercourse. Calf bile, if sprinkled on the womb during intercourse while purging, softens the hardness of the belly and reduces the discharge when the umbilical cord has been cut, and is entirely beneficial to the womb. They set the measure of the bile at the weight of a denarius mixed with a third of an ounce of celery and enough almond oil to seem sufficient, and they apply this in wool. Male calf bile is triturated with half its amount of honey and kept for the womb. If they eat calf meat roasted with birthwort <note>original: "aristolochia"</note> around the time of conception, they promise the birth of males. Calf marrow, boiled in wine and water with tallow, is beneficial for ulcerations of the womb. Likewise, fox fat and cat excrement applied with resin and rose oil. They consider it most useful to fumigate the womb with goat horn. The blood of wild goats with sea-palm removes hair. But the bile of other goats, when sprinkled, softens the callosity of the womb and causes conception after a purgation. The power of a <term>psilothrum</term> <gloss>hair-removing agent</gloss> is achieved in this way; it is kept applied for three days after the hairs are plucked. Midwives claim that an immense blood discharge is stopped by drinking goat urine, and if the dung is applied. The membrane of goats, aged in water after birth and taken as a drink in wine, expels the afterbirth. They consider it useful to fumigate the womb with the hair of kids. And in a discharge of blood, to drink the rennet or apply it with henbane seed. If the loins of a woman are rubbed with the blood of a black wild bull, Aeschines says that a weariness of sexual desire occurs. The same man says that goat urine mixed with nard is a drink for love, because of its potency. For infants, nothing is more useful than butter, by itself and with honey, both generally and for teething, and for the gums, and for mouth ulcers. A wolf's tooth tied on prevents the terrors of infants and diseases of teething. A wolf's skin does the same. Their largest teeth, when tied on, are said to provide an untiring run even for horses. The bowels of infants are stopped by applying hare rennet to the breast. Donkey liver, with a little all-heal <note>original: "panacea"</note> mixed in and instilled into the mouth, protects infants from the falling sickness <note>original: "comitialibus morbis"</note> and other diseases. They instruct that this be done for forty days. And an ass's skin thrown over them makes infants fearless. The teeth that first fall out from horses provide easy teething for infants when tied on. It is more effective if they have not touched the ground. Bull spleen is eaten in honey. It is also applied to pains of the spleen. For running ulcers, use it with honey. Calf spleen, boiled in wine, triturated, and applied, is for small mouth ulcers. Goat brain, passed through a gold ring, is instilled into infants before they are given milk, to prevent the falling sickness and other diseases of infants. Tied on with a cloth, goat dung keeps restless infants quiet, especially girls. Gums rubbed with goat's milk or hare's brain make teething easy. Cato believes that sleep is induced if hare is taken in food. The common people also believe it grants grace to the body for nine days, in a trivial way. Yet there must be some cause for such a strong persuasion. The magi say that sleep is induced by the bile of a sacrificed goat, applied to the eyes or placed under the pillow. Goat horn ash in myrtle oil, when rubbed on, inhibits sweat. Boar bile, when applied, stimulates intercourse. Likewise, drinking pig marrow. Ass's tallow mixed with the fat of a male goose, when applied. Likewise, the horse's act for Virgil <note>a reference to the classical belief in the aphrodisiacal properties of "hippomanes"</note>

<summary>This page covers various gynecological and pediatric medicinal recipes using animal products, such as hare, goat, donkey, and bull parts, to treat infertility, labor, and infant illnesses.</summary>
<keywords>womb, conception, infants, teething, labor, medical remedies, Pliny the Elder</keywords>
